figure.caption_tex: \numberline {1}{\ignorespaces Our explanatory target and evidence chain. Optimizer-specific trajectories create reached weight states and embeddings; weight and coordinate-level measurements become candidate explanations only if they predict full-corpus retrieval out of learning-rate dose. The crossed continuation estimates post-continuation state, operator, and interaction contrasts for one fixed checkpoint pair.}

\numberline {2}{\ignorespaces An observed weight-to-retrieval map, retaining all twelve runs and sixty checkpoints. The horizontal axis is cumulative hidden-weight displacement divided by current hidden-weight norm (joint Frobenius norms; logarithmic axis); the vertical axis is mean full-corpus nDCG@10 over fourteen BEIR tasks, in points. Lines connect the five measured stages in training order; open squares mark the final stage. All panels use identical axes. Learning-rate cells are not independent training seeds, and these descriptive curves do not replace the declared contrasts.}

\numberline {3}{\ignorespaces Dimension utility over the complete rate grid. (a) Final-state retention after shared random coordinate removal; the zero-removal value is one by definition. (b--d) Native-coordinate margin attribution at all five stages. Each optimizer curve averages all four rates and 14 tasks; (a) additionally averages 20 shared masks per nonzero fraction. The gray curve or horizontal line is the pretrained reference. Lines join measured points, not fitted trajectories. These are descriptive means, not confidence intervals or full-corpus retrieval scores; formal contrasts and rotation controls are reported separately.}

\numberline {4}{\ignorespaces Full-corpus retrieval through all five retained checkpoints, with every declared learning rate shown separately. Each point averages the same fourteen BEIR tasks; the shared vertical scale is nDCG@10 in points. Open squares mark the final stage. The curves show observed 20--100\% training progress and are not confidence intervals or fitted learning curves.}

table.caption_tex: \numberline {1}{\ignorespaces Final-stage retrieval over 14 decontaminated BEIR tasks, with simultaneous paired-task intervals for all three optimizer contrasts.}

\numberline {2}{\ignorespaces Every original weight-space predictor under four-fold leave-dose-index-out prediction. Decisions use exact MSE comparisons, not displayed RMSE. A missing correlation is undefined, not zero; baseline equivalence is distinct from an unidentified or numerically unresolved prediction.}

\numberline {3}{\ignorespaces Every original/exact counterpart under the same four held-out learning-rate doses. RMSE gain compares the exact predictor with the nuisance-only baseline; error difference is original-predictor RMSE minus exact-predictor RMSE. Decisions use exact MSE, not rounded display values. Dashes denote undefined comparisons. These are measurement-sensitivity comparisons, not uniformly pure approximation-error tests: entropy uses the full singular spectrum, and rank/entropy averages expose their nonzero-matrix denominators. Every declared correspondence and all four folds are retained. Undefined comparisons are not available-case averages. Predictive support is not causal mediation, statistical significance, equivalence, or evidence of useful embedding dimensions.}

\numberline {4}{\ignorespaces All nine final-stage co-primary contrasts, averaging every declared rate. One common-resample max-$T$ family covers all entries; task resampling does not estimate training-seed variation.}

\numberline {5}{\ignorespaces All four functional predictors beyond optimizer, stage and within-optimizer dose. Decisions use exact MSE comparisons; displayed RMSE is not a significance test. Undefined folds are retained, never pooled as available cases.}

\numberline {6}{\ignorespaces Complete post-result exploratory recipe-control sensitivity. Cells show pooled held-dose RMSE in nDCG@10 points (lower is better), and the number of improved folds. An asterisk marks strictly lower exact pooled MSE and improvement in at least three of four folds; it is not a significance test. D is cumulative weight displacement. All six comparator variants are retained.}

\numberline {7}{\ignorespaces Complete post-result exploratory recipe-control sensitivity. Cells show pooled held-dose RMSE in nDCG@10 points (lower is better), and the number of improved folds. An asterisk marks strictly lower exact pooled MSE and improvement in at least three of four folds; it is not a significance test. D is cumulative weight displacement. All six comparator variants are retained.}

\numberline {8}{\ignorespaces Prospective reset-state factorial on final decontaminated-BEIR nDCG@10. Effects average the fixed three order seeds and 14 tasks; intervals use the frozen two-way seed/task cluster bootstrap. These are marginal 95\% intervals, not simultaneous family-wise intervals.}
\numberline {9}{\ignorespaces How the analyses distinguish retrieval outcomes, predictive descriptors, and conditional continuation effects. Each comparison has a different scope of interpretation.}

actual_abstract.expanded_text:
Does an optimizer help retrieval through the weight states it reaches or the updates it applies?
We compare AdamW, Muon, and NorMuon from one pretrained DenseOn checkpoint on 500,000 shared
queries, following 12 configurations through five checkpoints and 14 decontaminated BEIR tasks.
Across the four-rate surface, Muon versus AdamW is inconclusive at +0.0016 [-0.0108, +0.0139] nDCG@10, and NorMuon versus AdamW is inconclusive at +0.0021 [-0.0089, +0.0130]. Weight-space maps reveal distinct trajectories, but coordinate-use
and held-out-rate prediction tests do not establish a recipe-robust geometric explanation.
Crossing two fixed reached states with reset continuation rules separates the source-state
comparison from the subsequent update-rule comparison.
At the 50K continuation endpoint, state, operator, and interaction contrasts are +0.0032 [+0.0005, +0.0068], -0.0053 [-0.0090, -0.0019], and +0.0021 [-0.0012, +0.0056] nDCG@10. They do not decompose the primary-training contrast.
